children.title: Reachable Direction-System Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Direction systems generated by directly reachable points and feasible arcs.

children.title: Radial Direction Geometry
children.top_down_role: Directions generated by direct displacement toward reachable points.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_C(\bar x)=\{\lambda(y-\bar x):\lambda\ge 0,\ y\in C\}\).

notation.meaning: radial cone of C at the reference point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the finite-dimensional, fixed-base radial cone convention and defines the positive-scaling hull explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The radial direction cone of \(C\) at \(\bar x\) is
\[
R_C(\bar x):=\{v\in\mathbb{R}^n:\text{there exists }t>0\text{ such that }\bar x+tv\in C\}=\{\lambda(y-\bar x):\lambda\ge 0,\ y\in C\}.
\]
A radial direction therefore requires one positive displacement from the fixed base point along its ray to reach \(C\), without requiring the intervening segment to lie in \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A radial direction is one whose ray from the reference point meets the set at some positive distance.
knowledge_statements.title: Radial Direction Geometry

children.title: Feasible-Direction Geometry
children.top_down_role: Directions supported by locally feasible arcs or motions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_C(\bar x)=\{v:\exists\varepsilon>0,\ \bar x+[0,\varepsilon]v\subset C\}\).

notation.meaning: cone of feasible directions of C at the reference point
line segment generated by v over the stated interval

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses exact straight-line feasibility, not asymptotic feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The feasible-direction cone of \(C\) at \(\bar x\) is
\[
F_C(\bar x):=\{v\in\mathbb{R}^n:\text{there exists }\varepsilon>0\text{ with }\bar x+tv\in C\text{ for every }t\in[0,\varepsilon]\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(v\) is feasible when an initial segment of the ray based at \(\bar x\) remains entirely in \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible direction keeps every sufficiently short straight-line displacement from the reference point inside the set.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Direction Geometry

children.title: Reachability Relations Between Direction Systems
children.top_down_role: Inclusion, closure, and local equivalence patterns linking the two systems.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_C(\bar x)\subset R_C(\bar x)\cap T_C(\bar x)\), with no general inclusion between \(R_C(\bar x)\) and \(T_C(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records only inclusions valid for arbitrary subsets of finite-dimensional space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every set \(C\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\bar x\in C\),
\[
F_C(\bar x)\subset R_C(\bar x)\quad\text{and}\quad F_C(\bar x)\subset T_C(\bar x).
\]
Neither \(R_C(\bar x)\subset T_C(\bar x)\) nor \(T_C(\bar x)\subset R_C(\bar x)\) holds for arbitrary nonconvex sets. If \(C\) is convex, then \(F_C(\bar x)=R_C(\bar x)\) and \(T_C(\bar x)=\operatorname{cl}R_C(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible directions are radial and contingent. Radial and contingent cones are otherwise incomparable, while convexity restores radial-feasible equality and tangent closure.
knowledge_statements.title: Reachability Relations Between Direction Systems

children.title: Direction-System Separation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Geometric settings where radial reachability fails to capture feasible arc behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete examples separate radial, contingent, and feasible direction systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(C_1=\{0,1\}\) at \(0\),
\[
1\in R_{C_1}(0)\setminus T_{C_1}(0),\qquad 1\notin F_{C_1}(0).
\]
For \(C_2=\{(0,0)\}\cup\{(1/k,1/k^2):k\in\mathbb{N}\}\) at \((0,0)\),
\[
(1,0)\in T_{C_2}(0)\setminus R_{C_2}(0),\qquad (1,0)\notin F_{C_2}(0).
\]
These examples separate the radial and contingent direction systems in both directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two elementary sets show that radial and contingent directions are mutually incomparable and that the displayed nonzero directions need not be feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Direction-System Separation Regimes

children.title: Bouligand–Contingent Tangent Geometry
children.top_down_role: Sequential outer tangent approximation and its local geometric role.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_C(\bar x)=\limsup_{t\downarrow0}(C-\bar x)/t\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional sequential outer tangent cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Bouligand-contingent tangent cone to \(C\) at \(\bar x\) is
\[
T_C(\bar x):=\left\{v\in\mathbb{R}^n:\begin{array}{l}\text{there exist }t_k\downarrow0\text{ and }v_k\to v\\\text{such that }\bar x+t_kv_k\in C\text{ for every }k\end{array}\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(T_C(\bar x)=\limsup_{t\downarrow0}(C-\bar x)/t\), or \(v\in T_C(\bar x)\) exactly when \(\liminf_{t\downarrow0}d(\bar x+tv,C)/t=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The contingent cone contains directions reachable by set points along some vanishing sequence of step sizes and asymptotically matching velocities.
knowledge_statements.title: Bouligand–Contingent Tangent Geometry

children.title: Uniform-Approach Tangent Pair
children.top_down_role: Inner and robust tangent constructions based on uniform approach behavior.

children.title: Adjacent Tangent Geometry
children.top_down_role: Inner tangent behavior tied to prescribed approach sequences.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_C^A(\bar x)=\liminf_{t\downarrow0}(C-\bar x)/t\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the fixed-base inner-limit definition of adjacent tangency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The adjacent tangent cone to \(C\) at \(\bar x\) is
\[
T_C^A(\bar x):=\liminf_{t\downarrow0}\frac{C-\bar x}{t}=\left\{v:\lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{d(\bar x+tv,C)}{t}=0\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(v\in T_C^A(\bar x)\) when, for every sequence \(t_k\downarrow0\), there exist \(v_k\to v\) satisfying \(\bar x+t_kv_k\in C\). Thus approximation must work along every vanishing step-size sequence, while the base point remains fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adjacent direction can be approximated from the fixed base point along every sequence of vanishing step sizes.
knowledge_statements.title: Adjacent Tangent Geometry

children.title: Ursescu Tangent Geometry
children.top_down_role: Uniformly approachable tangent behavior across nearby scales.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_C^U(\bar x)=\liminf_{t\downarrow0}(C-\bar x)/t\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the common convention identifying Ursescu and adjacent fixed-base inner tangents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the fixed-base convention, the Ursescu tangent cone is
\[
T_C^U(\bar x):=\left\{v\in\mathbb{R}^n:\text{for every }t_k\downarrow0\text{ there are }v_k\to v\text{ with }\bar x+t_kv_k\in C\right\}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
T_C^U(\bar x)=\liminf_{t\downarrow0}\frac{C-\bar x}{t}=\left\{v:\lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{d(\bar x+tv,C)}{t}=0\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Ursescu cone consists of directions attainable asymptotically for every vanishing step-size sequence; under this convention it is the adjacent cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Ursescu Tangent Geometry

children.title: Uniform-Approach Comparison
children.top_down_role: Relative robustness and inclusion patterns of the adjacent and Ursescu constructions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_C^C(\bar x)\subset T_C^A(\bar x)=T_C^U(\bar x)\subset T_C(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison under the fixed-base adjacent/Ursescu convention.

source_refs.locator: B. Normal Cones and Clarke Regularity p. 199

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
With the adjacent and Ursescu cones defined by the fixed-base inner limit,
\[
T_C^C(\bar x)\subset T_C^A(\bar x)=T_C^U(\bar x)\subset T_C(\bar x).
\]
Each inclusion can be strict for a closed nonconvex set. If \(C\) is convex, then
\[
T_C^C(\bar x)=T_C^A(\bar x)=T_C^U(\bar x)=T_C(\bar x)=\operatorname{cl}\{\lambda(y-\bar x):\lambda\ge0,\ y\in C\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clarke tangency lies inside the coincident fixed-base adjacent and Ursescu cones, which lie inside contingent tangency; convex sets eliminate these differences.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform-Approach Comparison

source_witnesses.locator: B. Normal Cones and Clarke Regularity p. 199

children.title: Tangent-Robustness Gaps
children.top_down_role: Local regimes where sequence-dependent and uniform tangent behavior diverge.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_C^C(\bar x)=\{0\}\subsetneq T_C^A(\bar x)=T_C(\bar x)=C\).

notation.meaning: union of the two coordinate axes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A crossing set exhibits failure of robustness under moving base points.

source_refs.locator: B. Normal Cones and Clarke Regularity p. 199

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the union of the coordinate axes
\[
C=\{(a,0):a\in\mathbb{R}\}\cup\{(0,b):b\in\mathbb{R}\}
\]
at \(\bar x=(0,0)\), the fixed-base and moving-base tangent systems satisfy
\[
T_C^C(\bar x)=\{0\}\subsetneq T_C^A(\bar x)=T_C(\bar x)=C.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the crossing of two axes, the fixed-base adjacent and contingent cones contain both axes, while the Clarke cone is reduced to zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Tangent-Robustness Gaps

source_witnesses.locator: B. Normal Cones and Clarke Regularity p. 199

children.title: Clarke Tangent Geometry
children.top_down_role: Uniformized and convexified tangent geometry.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_C^C(\bar x)=\{v:\lim_{x\to_C\bar x,\,t\downarrow0}d(x+tv,C)/t=0\}\).

notation.meaning: convergence to the reference point through C

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional uniformized Clarke tangent cone.

source_refs.locator: B. Normal Cones and Clarke Regularity p. 199

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Clarke tangent cone to \(C\) at \(\bar x\) is
\[
T_C^C(\bar x):=\left\{v\in\mathbb{R}^n:\lim_{\substack{x\to_C\bar x\\t\downarrow0}}\frac{d(x+tv,C)}{t}=0\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, for every \(x_k\to_C\bar x\) and every \(t_k\downarrow0\), there exist \(v_k\to v\) such that \(x_k+t_kv_k\in C\). The set \(T_C^C(\bar x)\) is a closed convex cone contained in \(T_C(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Clarke tangent direction remains asymptotically feasible for every nearby base point and every vanishing step-size sequence; the resulting cone is closed and convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Clarke Tangent Geometry

source_witnesses.locator: B. Normal Cones and Clarke Regularity p. 199

children.title: Localized Tangent Geometry
children.top_down_role: Tangent constructions localized by direction, ambient set, face, or active structure.

children.title: Directional Tangent Cones
children.top_down_role: Tangency localized around a selected approach direction.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_C(\bar x;d)=\limsup_{t\downarrow0,\,d'\to d,\,\bar x+td'\in C}T_C(\bar x+td')\).

notation.meaning: Bouligand tangent cone at a nearby point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selects a directional outer limit of nearby Bouligand cones; conventions vary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a selected approach direction \(d\in T_C(\bar x)\), define the directionally localized tangent cone by
\[
T_C(\bar x;d):=\limsup_{\substack{t\downarrow0,\ d'\to d\\\bar x+td'\in C}}T_C(\bar x+td').
\]
Thus \(w\in T_C(\bar x;d)\) exactly when there exist \(t_k\downarrow0\), \(d_k\to d\), and \(w_k\to w\) such that \(x_k:=\bar x+t_kd_k\in C\) and \(w_k\in T_C(x_k)\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directional tangent cone collects limiting tangent directions at points approaching the reference point specifically along a selected first-order direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Directional Tangent Cones

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed construction is a plausible directional outer limit of nearby Bouligand cones, but directional tangent terminology has materially different conventions in the literature. With no citation, the exact definition intended by this leaf cannot be established reliably.

children.title: Relative Tangent Cones
children.top_down_role: Tangency relative to an ambient set or locally active component.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{C\mid Q}(\bar x):=T_{C\cap Q}(\bar x)\subset T_C(\bar x)\cap T_Q(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: tangent cone to C relative to the ambient set Q

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses intersection localization as the relative-tangent convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Bouligand tangent cone to \(C\) relative to an ambient or active set \(Q\) at \(\bar x\) is
\[
T_{C\mid Q}(\bar x):=T_{C\cap Q}(\bar x)=\limsup_{t\downarrow0}\frac{(C\cap Q)-\bar x}{t}.
\]
Equivalently, \(v\in T_{C\mid Q}(\bar x)\) when there are \(t_k\downarrow0\) and \(v_k\to v\) with \(\bar x+t_kv_k\in C\cap Q\). Always \(T_{C\mid Q}(\bar x)\subset T_C(\bar x)\cap T_Q(\bar x)\); equality requires additional intersection regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative tangency restricts approximating points to both the set and a chosen ambient or active set; it is generally smaller than intersecting tangent cones.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative Tangent Cones

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The intersection-localized construction and stated inclusion are mathematically coherent, but relative tangent cone is not a uniquely standardized name for this construction. A source is required to establish that this is the convention intended by the exact leaf container.

children.title: Linearized Cones
children.top_down_role: Direction systems inherited from first-order constraint representations.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_C(\bar x)=\{d:\nabla g_i(\bar x)^\top d\le 0\ (i\in I(\bar x)),\ \nabla h_j(\bar x)^\top d=0\ (j=1,\ldots,q)\}\).

notation.meaning: active inequality indices at the feasible point
linearized cone to the represented feasible set
feasible set defined by the displayed constraints

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth equality-and-inequality representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(x)\le 0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ h_j(x)=0\ (j=1,\ldots,q)\}\), let \(\bar x\in C\), and define \(I(\bar x)=\{i:g_i(\bar x)=0\}\). The linearized cone generated by this constraint representation is
\[
L_C(\bar x):=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:\nabla g_i(\bar x)^\top d\le 0\ \text{for every }i\in I(\bar x),\ \nabla h_j(\bar x)^\top d=0\ \text{for every }j\}.
\]
It depends on the chosen representation and always contains every differentiable feasible-arc velocity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linearized cone consists of directions satisfying the first-order versions of all active inequalities and equalities at the feasible point.
knowledge_statements.title: Linearized Cones

children.title: Critical Cones
children.top_down_role: Feasible directions organized by active first-order optimality information.

assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is feasible and first-order stationary
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K(\bar x)=L_C(\bar x)\cap\{\nabla f(\bar x)\}^{\perp}\).

notation.meaning: critical cone at the stationary point
linearized cone of the constraint representation
gradient of the objective at the reference point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth nonlinear program at a first-order stationary feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\le 0\) and \(h_j(x)=0\), let \(\bar x\) be feasible and let \(L_C(\bar x)\) be the linearized cone. The critical cone is
\[
K(\bar x):=\{d\in L_C(\bar x):\nabla f(\bar x)^\top d=0\}.
\]
Thus it retains precisely those linearized feasible directions along which the objective has zero first-order change. If stationarity is represented by multipliers, this equality combines with complementary slackness to organize directions according to the active constraints carrying positive multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The critical cone contains linearized feasible directions along which a stationary objective has zero first-order change.
knowledge_statements.title: Critical Cones

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed formula is a standard NLP critical-cone formulation under a suitable stationarity or multiplier condition, but the record does not define what first-order stationary means relative to the representation. The cited general variational-geometry page is not sufficiently specific to verify this formula and its multiplier interpretation.

children.title: Tangent–Linearization Gaps
children.top_down_role: Failure boundaries between intrinsic tangency and representation-derived directions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_C(0)=\{0\}\subsetneq L_C(0)=\mathbb R\).

notation.meaning: cone obtained by linearizing the displayed constraint

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete degeneracy showing failure of first-order constraint linearization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any differentiable constraint representation, feasible-arc velocities satisfy \(T_C(\bar x)\subseteq L_C(\bar x)\), but equality can fail without an appropriate constraint qualification. Consider
\[
C=\{x\in\mathbb R:x^2\le 0\}=\{0\},\qquad \bar x=0.
\]
Because \(C\) is a singleton, \(T_C(0)=\{0\}\). The active constraint has derivative \(g'(0)=0\), so its linearization imposes \(0d\le 0\) and hence \(L_C(0)=\mathbb R\). Therefore the representation-derived cone strictly overestimates intrinsic tangency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degenerate constraint can yield every direction after linearization even though the feasible set has only the zero tangent direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Tangent–Linearization Gaps

children.title: Tangential Derivability
children.top_down_role: Regularity regimes in which outer and inner tangent approximations agree.

children.title: Geometrically Derivable Sets
children.top_down_role: Sets admitting coherent arc-based and sequential tangent models.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is locally closed at \(\bar x\in C\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is geometrically derivable at \(\bar x\) exactly when every \(v\in T_C(\bar x)\) is the right derivative of a feasible arc.

notation.meaning: Bouligand contingent cone to the set
feasible arc realizing a tangent direction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arc characterization of geometric derivability in Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A set \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is geometrically derivable at \(\bar x\in C\) if, for every \(v\in T_C(\bar x)\), there exist \(\varepsilon>0\) and an arc \(\gamma:[0,\varepsilon)\to C\) such that
\[
\gamma(0)=\bar x,\qquad \lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{\gamma(t)-\bar x}{t}=v.
\]
Equivalently, every direction admitted by the sequential contingent construction is realized as the right derivative of a single feasible arc. The property is local at \(\bar x\); a set is geometrically derivable when it has this property at each of its points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set is geometrically derivable when every contingent direction is realized by the initial velocity of one feasible arc.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometrically Derivable Sets

children.title: Tangential Nonregularity
children.top_down_role: Disagreement among radial, contingent, adjacent, and Clarke tangent constructions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_C^C(\bar x)=\{0\}\subsetneq T_C(\bar x)=T_C^A(\bar x)=R_C(\bar x)=C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Crossing axes illustrate loss of robust tangency at a branch point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
C=(\mathbb R\times\{0\})\cup(\{0\}\times\mathbb R),\qquad \bar x=(0,0).
\]
Every direction lying on either coordinate axis is radial and is available at every positive scale, so
\[
R_C(\bar x)=T_C(\bar x)=T_C^A(\bar x)=C.
\]
However, a nonzero axial direction cannot remain tangent when the base point approaches \(\bar x\) along the other axis. Consequently the robust Clarke tangent cone is \(T_C^C(\bar x)=\{0\}\). Thus contingent, adjacent, and radial tangency can agree while differing strictly from Clarke tangency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the crossing of two axes, ordinary sequential and radial tangents contain both axes, whereas the robust Clarke tangent contains only zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Tangential Nonregularity

children.title: Convex Normal Geometry
children.top_down_role: Normal geometry governed by convex support and separation.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_C(\bar x)=T_C(\bar x)^\circ=\{v:\langle v,x-\bar x\rangle\le0\ \forall x\in C\}\).

notation.meaning: convex normal cone to the set
tangent cone to the convex set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean convex normal cone and tangent-polar duality.

source_refs.locator: C. Smooth Manifolds and Convex Sets p. 202

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) and \(\bar x\in C\), its convex normal cone is
\[
N_C(\bar x):=\{v\in\mathbb R^n:\langle v,x-\bar x\rangle\le0\ \text{for every }x\in C\}.
\]
If the negative polar of a cone \(K\) is \(K^\circ:=\{v:\langle v,d\rangle\le0\ \text{for every }d\in K\}\), then
\[
N_C(\bar x)=T_C(\bar x)^\circ.
\]
Thus global supporting inequalities and the polar of local feasible directions define the same normal geometry for convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed convex set, normal vectors globally support the set at the point, and the normal cone is the tangent cone's negative polar.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Normal Geometry

source_witnesses.locator: C. Smooth Manifolds and Convex Sets p. 202

children.title: Regular–Fréchet Normal Geometry
children.top_down_role: Local supporting geometry associated with regular first-order behavior.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat N_C(\bar x)=\{v:\limsup_{x\to\bar x,\ x\in C\setminus\{\bar x\}}\langle v,x-\bar x\rangle/\|x-\bar x\|\le0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean regular normal defined by first-order local support.

source_refs.locator: B. Normal Cones and Clarke Regularity p. 199

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) and \(\bar x\in C\), the regular, or Fréchet, normal cone is
\[
\widehat N_C(\bar x):=\left\{v\in\mathbb R^n:\limsup_{\substack{x\to\bar x\\x\in C,\ x\ne\bar x}}\frac{\langle v,x-\bar x\rangle}{\|x-\bar x\|}\le0\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(v\in\widehat N_C(\bar x)\) precisely when
\[
\langle v,x-\bar x\rangle\le o(\|x-\bar x\|)\quad\text{as }x\to\bar x\text{ within }C.
\]
This cone records vectors that support the set to first order at the reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regular normal has nonpositive inner product with nearby feasible displacements up to an error negligible relative to the displacement length.
knowledge_statements.title: Regular–Fréchet Normal Geometry

source_witnesses.locator: B. Normal Cones and Clarke Regularity p. 199

children.title: Proximal Normal Geometry
children.top_down_role: Normal directions generated by local nearest-point and supporting-ball geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is locally closed at \(\bar x\in C\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v\in N_C^P(\bar x)\) exactly when \(\langle v,x-\bar x\rangle\le(\sigma/2)\|x-\bar x\|^2\) locally for some \(\sigma\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean metric projection onto the set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent projection and quadratic-support descriptions in Euclidean space.

source_refs.locator: B. Normal Cones and Clarke Regularity p. 199

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a locally closed set \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) and \(\bar x\in C\), a vector \(v\) is proximal normal at \(\bar x\) when there exists \(r>0\) such that \(\bar x\in P_C(\bar x+rv)\). Equivalently, after rescaling the parameter, there exist \(\sigma\ge0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) satisfying
\[
\langle v,x-\bar x\rangle\le\frac{\sigma}{2}\|x-\bar x\|^2\qquad\text{for every }x\in C\cap U.
\]
The collection of all such vectors is the proximal normal cone \(N_C^P(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal normal points from a nearest feasible point toward an exterior center and equivalently provides local quadratic support.
knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Normal Geometry

source_witnesses.locator: B. Normal Cones and Clarke Regularity p. 199

children.title: Limiting–Mordukhovich Normal Geometry
children.top_down_role: Sequential limiting normal geometry for nonconvex sets.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is locally closed at \(\bar x\in C\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_C(\bar x)=\operatorname*{Limsup}_{x\to\bar x,\ x\in C}\widehat N_C(x)\).

notation.meaning: regular normal cone at a nearby point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong sequential limiting construction in finite-dimensional space.

source_refs.locator: B. Normal Cones and Clarke Regularity p. 199

source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a locally closed set \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) and \(\bar x\in C\), the limiting, or Mordukhovich, normal cone is
\[
N_C(\bar x):=\left\{v:\exists x_k\to\bar x,\ x_k\in C,\ \exists v_k\to v,\ v_k\in\widehat N_C(x_k)\right\}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
N_C(\bar x)=\operatorname*{Limsup}_{\substack{x\to\bar x\\x\in C}}\widehat N_C(x).
\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact bipolar relation for convex tangent and normal cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[T_C(x):=\overline{\{t(z-x):t\geq0,\ z\in C\}},\qquad N_C(x):=\{x^*\in X^*: \langle x^*,z-x\rangle\leq0\ \forall z\in C\}.\]
For a cone \(K\), set \(K^\circ:=\{x^*: \langle x^*,h\rangle\leq0\ \forall h\in K\}\), with the analogous prepolar for subsets of \(X^*\). Then convexity yields the exact relations \(N_C(x)=T_C(x)^\circ\) and \(T_C(x)=N_C(x)^\circ\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex set, its tangent and normal cones determine one another exactly by negative polarity.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The contingent tangent cone is
\[T_C(x):=\left\{h:\exists t_k\downarrow0,\ \exists x_k\in C,\ x_k\to x,\ \frac{x_k-x}{t_k}\to h\right\}.\]
The Fréchet normal cone satisfies the exact local polarity formula
\[\widehat N_C(x)=T_C(x)^\circ=\{x^*\in X^*: \langle x^*,h\rangle\leq0\ \forall h\in T_C(x)\}.\]
This equality concerns regular normals at the fixed point; it does not assert that the generally nonconvex limiting normal cone is the polar of \(T_C(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a finite-dimensional normed space, regular normals at a point are exactly the covectors nonpositive on every contingent tangent direction there.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

\[N_C(\bar x):=\operatorname*{Limsup}_{x\to_C\bar x}\widehat N_C(x)=\left\{x^*: \exists x_k\to_C\bar x,\ \exists x_k^*\to x^*,\ x_k^*\in\widehat N_C(x_k)\right\}.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the Clarke normal cone by convexifying the limiting normal cone:
\[N_C^{\mathrm C}(\bar x):=\overline{\operatorname{co}}N_C(\bar x).\]
For the Clarke tangent cone \(T_C^{\mathrm C}(\bar x)\), exact polarity is recovered:
\[N_C^{\mathrm C}(\bar x)=T_C^{\mathrm C}(\bar x)^\circ,\qquad T_C^{\mathrm C}(\bar x)=N_C^{\mathrm C}(\bar x)^\circ.\]
Both cones are closed and convex. Convexification can strictly enlarge the limiting normal cone and can strictly shrink the contingent tangent cone when \(C\) is nonconvex.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the union of the coordinate axes at the origin,
\[T_C(\bar x)=C,\qquad \widehat N_C(\bar x)=T_C(\bar x)^\circ=\{0\}.\]
Normals obtained along either punctured axis give

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal information generated by an attained nearest-point projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \(x\in P_C(y)\), then comparison of squared distances gives
\[\langle y-x,z-x\rangle\leq\frac12\|z-x\|^2\qquad\text{for every }z\in C.\]
Consequently \(y-x\in N_C^P(x)\). If \(y\notin C\), the normalized direction \((y-x)/\|y-x\|\) is a nonzero unit proximal normal. The assertion is conditional on attainment of the distance; a general nonconvex closed subset of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space need not admit a nearest point for every \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Whenever a nearest point exists, the displacement from it to the external point is a proximal normal.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance-attaining points generate normalized proximal normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(d_C(y):=\inf_{z\in C}\|y-z\|\). If \(x\in P_C(y)\) and \(y\notin C\), then
\[d_C(y)=\|y-x\|>0,\qquad u:=\frac{y-x}{d_C(y)}\in N_C^P(x),\qquad\|u\|=1.\]
Moreover, for every \(z\in C\),
\[\langle u,z-x\rangle\leq\frac{1}{2d_C(y)}\|z-x\|^2.\]
Thus an attained distance value determines both a nearest boundary point and a normalized proximal supporting direction there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An attained positive distance identifies a nearest point and a unit proximal normal pointing toward the external point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent projection and supporting-ball representations of a proximal-normal direction.

The open ball centered at \(x+ru\) with radius \(r\) supports \(C\) at \(x\) exactly when
\[B(x+ru,r)\cap C=\varnothing.\]
Because \(\|x-(x+ru)\|=r\), this condition is equivalent to \(x\in P_C(x+ru)\). In that case \(u\in N_C^P(x)\), with \(r\) serving as a proximal-support parameter, and
\[\langle u,z-x\rangle\leq\frac{1}{2r}\|z-x\|^2\qquad\text{for every }z\in C.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A radius-r open ball centered at x+ru avoids the set and touches it at x exactly when x is a nearest point to the center; this makes u a proximal normal supported with radius r.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Tangent Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-inequality representation of tangent cones to polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have rows \(a_i^T\), let \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and let \(P=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:Az\leq b\}\neq\varnothing\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a polyhedron described by finitely many inequalities, its tangent cone consists exactly of directions satisfying the homogeneous forms of the inequalities active at the base point.

children.title: Face Geometry

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is a face exactly when every segment of \(C\) whose relative interior meets \(F\) has both endpoints in \(F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard finite-dimensional definition of a convex face.

source_refs.locator: A. Convex Sets and Functions p. 38

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The set \(F\) is a face of \(C\) if, for every \(x,y\in C\) and every \(t\in(0,1)\), the implication \(tx+(1-t)y\in F\Rightarrow x,y\in F\) holds. Equivalently, whenever the relative interior of a line segment contained in \(C\) intersects \(F\), the entire segment lies in \(F\). A face is proper when \(F\ne C\), and it is exposed when there exists \(a\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \(F=\operatorname*{argmax}_{z\in C}\langle a,z\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex subset is a face when containing an interior point of a segment in the ambient convex set forces it to contain both endpoints.
knowledge_statements.title: Face Geometry

source_witnesses.locator: A. Convex Sets and Functions p. 38

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{face}_C(S)=\bigcap\{F:F\text{ is a face of }C,\ S\subset F\}\) is the unique smallest face containing \(S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal faces of finite-dimensional convex sets.

source_refs.locator: A. Convex Sets and Functions p. 38

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The minimal face of \(C\) containing \(S\) is \[\operatorname{face}_C(S):=\bigcap\{F\subset C:F\text{ is a face of }C\text{ and }S\subset F\}.\] It is itself a face, contains \(S\), and is contained in every face containing \(S\). In particular, for each \(x\in C\), the point \(x\) belongs to \(\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{face}_C(x))\); hence the relative interiors of the nonempty faces partition \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimal face containing a set is the intersection of all faces containing it; every point lies in the relative interior of its unique minimal face.

children.title: Facial-Reduction Geometry
children.top_down_role: Reduced geometric representations obtained by passing to lower-dimensional faces.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone.
\(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear and \(\{x\in K:Ax=b\}\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reductions preserve feasibility and terminate at a face containing a feasible point in its relative interior.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact facial reduction for a feasible finite-dimensional conic system.

source_refs.locator: D. Cones and Convex Sets p. 118

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(K_0:=K\). While no \(x\in\operatorname{ri}K_i\) satisfies \(Ax=b\), choose \(y_i\in\mathbb R^m\) such that \(z_i:=A^*y_i\in K_i^*\setminus K_i^\perp\) and \(\langle y_i,b\rangle=0\), then set \(K_{i+1}:=K_i\cap z_i^\perp\). Each feasible point lies in \(K_{i+1}\), and \(K_{i+1}\) is a proper exposed face of \(K_i\). Stop at the first \(r\) admitting \(x\in\operatorname{ri}K_r\) with \(Ax=b\), and output \(K_r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly intersect the current cone with exposing hyperplanes that contain the feasible set until the reduced conic system satisfies relative-interior feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Facial-Reduction Geometry

children.title: Face-Localized Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Concentration of constraint degeneracy within proper facial strata.

assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone and \(Ax=b\) is feasible.
\(F\) is the minimal face of \(K\) containing the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Face-localized degeneracy occurs exactly when \(A(\operatorname{span}F)\ne\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constraint degeneracy measured after restriction to the minimal feasible face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The conic system is face-locally degenerate when the constraint map restricted to the linear hull of its minimal feasible face is not surjective: \[A(\operatorname{span}F)\ne\mathbb R^m.\] In finite dimensions this is equivalent to the existence of \(y\in\mathbb R^m\setminus\{0\}\) satisfying \(A^*y\in(\operatorname{span}F)^\perp\). Thus the multiplier direction \(y\) is invisible to every feasible first-order displacement remaining in \(F\), even if redundant ambient directions have already been removed by facial reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degeneracy localized to the minimal feasible face means the equality constraints fail to be surjective on that face’s linear span.
knowledge_statements.title: Face-Localized Degeneracy

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At every \(x\in M\), \[N_M(x)=T_M(x)^\perp,\qquad T_M(x)=N_M(x)^\perp,\qquad \mathbb R^n=T_M(x)\oplus N_M(x).\] Hence every \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) has a unique decomposition \(v=v_T+v_N\), where \(v_T\in T_M(x)\), \(v_N\in N_M(x)\), and \(\langle v_T,v_N\rangle=0\). abla g(x),vangle=0\}.\] The Bouligand tangent cone is \[T_C(x)=\{v:\langle

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(K^\circ:=\{y\in\mathbb R^n:\langle y,z\rangle\le0\text{ for all }z\in K\}\). children.title: Structured-Cone Geometry
children.top_down_role: Local variational structure arising from cones with additional algebraic organization.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\subset\mathbb R^n\) is a closed convex cone invariant under coordinate permutations.
\(K=\{X\in\mathbb S^n:\lambda(X)\in Q\}\), with eigenvalues listed in nonincreasing order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tangent and normal geometry of \(K\) is obtained from the corresponding spectral-vector geometry of \(Q\), with compatibility inside repeated-eigenvalue subspaces.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral realization of orthogonally invariant structured matrix cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The cone \(K\) is orthogonally invariant: \(X\in K\Rightarrow UXU^\mathsf T\in K\) for every orthogonal \(U\). If \(X=U\operatorname{Diag}(\lambda(X))U^\mathsf T\), then its structured normal geometry is represented by \[N_K(X)=\{U\operatorname{Diag}(y)U^\mathsf T:y\in N_Q(\lambda(X)),\ U\text{ diagonalizes }X\},\] where the choice of \(U\) accounts for rotations within repeated-eigenvalue eigenspaces. Thus faces, complementarity, and degeneracy of \(K\) are governed jointly by the facial geometry of \(Q\) and the eigenvalue-multiplicity pattern of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthogonally invariant matrix cone inherits its local geometry from an eigenvalue cone, with repeated eigenvalues introducing additional rotational structure.
knowledge_statements.title: Structured-Cone Geometry

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Cone Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional orthogonally invariant cones of real symmetric matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(X\in\mathbb{S}^n\), let \(\lambda(X)=(\lambda_1(X),\ldots,\lambda_n(X))\) list its eigenvalues in nonincreasing order. The spectral lift of \(C\) is
\[\mathcal{K}_C:=\{X\in\mathbb{S}^n:\lambda(X)\in C\}.\]
Permutation invariance makes the construction independent of eigenvalue labeling, and \(X\in\mathcal{K}_C\) implies \(QXQ^{\mathsf T}\in\mathcal{K}_C\) for every orthogonal \(Q\). Under the stated assumptions, \(\mathcal{K}_C\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A permutation-invariant closed convex eigenvalue cone lifts to a closed convex cone of symmetric matrices invariant under orthogonal similarity.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a closed convex cone invariant under coordinate permutations.
\(\mathbb{S}^n\) carries the trace inner product \(\langle X,Y\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(XY)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{K}_C=\lambda^{-1}(C)\) is a closed convex cone in \(\mathbb{S}^n\) and is invariant under orthogonal similarity.

notation.meaning: Vector of eigenvalues of a symmetric matrix, arranged in nonincreasing order.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth rank stratification of the real positive semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(\mathcal{S}_r:=\{Y\in\mathbb{S}_+^n:\operatorname{rank}Y=r\}\), and complete \(U_r\) to an orthogonal matrix \([U_r\ U_0]\). Then \(\mathcal{S}_r\) is a smooth embedded manifold of dimension \(r(2n-r+1)/2\). Its tangent space at \(X\) is
\[T_{\mathcal{S}_r}(X)=\{U_rAU_r^{\mathsf T}+U_rBU_0^{\mathsf T}+U_0B^{\mathsf T}U_r^{\mathsf T}:A\in\mathbb{S}^r,\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times(n-r)}\}.\]
Thus the lower-right nullspace block vanishes along first-order motions that remain in the same rank stratum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive semidefinite matrices of fixed rank form a smooth manifold whose tangent matrices have zero nullspace-to-nullspace block.
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Cone Strata

children.title: Spectral Degeneracy Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Local regimes where eigenvalue multiplicity or rank loss changes cone geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Degeneracy Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary degeneracy for the real positive semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The interior and boundary of the positive semidefinite cone satisfy
\[\operatorname{int}\mathbb{S}_+^n=\{X\in\mathbb{S}^n:\lambda_{\min}(X)>0\},\qquad \operatorname{bd}\mathbb{S}_+^n=\{X\in\mathbb{S}_+^n:\lambda_{\min}(X)=0\}.\]
Consequently, a positive semidefinite matrix lies on the spectral degeneracy boundary exactly when it is singular. The boundary is the disjoint union \(\bigcup_{r=0}^{n-1}\mathcal{S}_r\); transitions between these strata occur when one or more positive eigenvalues approach zero, changing the kernel dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The semidefinite boundary consists exactly of singular positive semidefinite matrices and decomposes into rank strata below full rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\in\operatorname{bd}\mathbb{S}_+^n\iff\lambda_{\min}(X)=0\iff\operatorname{rank}X<n\).

notation.meaning: Smallest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix.

children.title: Branched Set Geometry Family

children.title: Finite-Union Geometry
children.top_down_role: Branch-sensitive tangent and normal geometry of locally finite unions.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Union Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bouligand tangent geometry of a finite union of closed sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a closed set \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(x\in D\), define its Bouligand tangent cone by
\[T_D(x):=\{u\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exists\,t_k\downarrow0,\ u_k\to u,\ x+t_ku_k\in D\}.\]
For the finite union \(C=\bigcup_{i=1}^m C_i\), only branches in \(I(x)\) contribute locally, and
\[T_C(x)=\bigcup_{i\in I(x)}T_{C_i}(x).\]
The resulting tangent cone can be nonconvex even when every branch is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Bouligand tangent cone to a finite union is the union of the tangent cones of all branches active at the reference point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_C(x)=\bigcup_{i\in I(x)}T_{C_i}(x)\).

notation.meaning: Indices of branches containing the reference point.

children.title: Piecewise-Smooth Geometry
children.top_down_role: Local geometry assembled from smooth pieces and active branches.

assumptions_latex: \(M_1,\ldots,M_m\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) are embedded \(C^1\) manifolds that are locally closed near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_C(x)=\bigcup_{i\in I(x)}T_{M_i}(x)\).

notation.meaning: Active smooth pieces at the reference point.
Classical tangent space to an active manifold.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local finite unions of embedded smooth manifolds.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Each active piece has the classical tangent space
\[T_{M_i}(x)=\{u:\nabla h_i(x)u=0\}\]
whenever \(M_i\) is locally represented as \(\{y:h_i(y)=0\}\) with \(\nabla h_i(x)\) surjective. The piecewise-smooth union therefore has the branch representation
\[T_C(x)=\bigcup_{i\in I(x)}T_{M_i}(x).\]
At a point belonging to one piece, this is an ordinary linear tangent space; at an intersection of pieces, it is generally a nonconvex union of distinct linear spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite piecewise-smooth set has a tangent cone equal to the union of tangent spaces of its active smooth pieces.
knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Smooth Geometry

children.title: Complementarity-Set Geometry
children.top_down_role: Local set geometry induced by complementarity-type constraints.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_Q(a,b)\) is determined coordinatewise by the three active complementarity cases.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise tangent geometry of the nonnegative complementarity set.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A direction \((\alpha,\beta)\) belongs to \(T_Q(a,b)\) exactly when, for every coordinate \(i\),
\[a_i>0\Rightarrow\beta_i=0,\qquad b_i>0\Rightarrow\alpha_i=0,\qquad a_i=b_i=0\Rightarrow(\alpha_i,\beta_i)\in Q_1,\]
where \(Q_1:=\{(s,t)\in\mathbb{R}^2:s\ge0,\ t=0\}\cup\{(s,t)\in\mathbb{R}^2:s=0,\ t\ge0\}\). Thus biactive coordinates generate two alternative tangent branches, while strictly complementary coordinates impose one linear equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementarity tangents are coordinatewise: strict complementarity fixes one directional component, while a biactive coordinate permits either nonnegative axis.
knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity-Set Geometry

children.title: Disjunctive-Set Geometry
children.top_down_role: Local geometry assembled from logical alternatives or finite branches.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive-Set Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite unions of closed polyhedral disjuncts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each active disjunct \(D_i\), its tangent cone \(T_{D_i}(z)\) is a closed convex polyhedral cone. The tangent geometry of the disjunctive set is
\[T_D(z)=\bigcup_{i\in I(z)}T_{D_i}(z).\]
Hence \(T_D(z)\) is a finite union of polyhedral cones, although it need not itself be convex. If \(D_i=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^q:A_i y\le b_i\}\), then
\[T_{D_i}(z)=\{w\in\mathbb{R}^q:(A_iw)_j\le0\text{ for every }j\text{ with }(A_iz)_j=(b_i)_j\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A disjunctive polyhedral set has a tangent cone equal to the finite union of the active disjuncts' polyhedral tangent cones.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_D(z)=\bigcup_{i\in I(z)}T_{D_i}(z)\), with every \(T_{D_i}(z)\) polyhedral.

notation.meaning: Indices of disjuncts containing the reference point.

children.title: Active-Branch Tangent Systems
children.top_down_role: Branch-indexed tangent behavior at disjunctive reference points.

assumptions_latex: \(D=\bigcup_{i=1}^mD_i\) is a finite union of closed sets and \(F(\bar x)\in D\).
The mapping \(x\mapsto F(x)-D\) is metrically subregular at \((\bar x,0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{F^{-1}(D)}(\bar x)=\bigcup_{i\in I(F(\bar x))}\{u:\nabla F(\bar x)u\in T_{D_i}(F(\bar x))\}\).

notation.meaning: Active disjunct indices at a point of the image space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact tangent linearization under metric subregularity.

source_refs.locator: 4.4 Sensitivity Analysis for Variational Systems p. 421
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X:=\{x:F(x)\in D\}\) and \(z:=F(\bar x)\). Metric subregularity yields the exact tangent linearization
\[T_X(\bar x)=\{u:\nabla F(\bar x)u\in T_D(z)\}.\]
Because \(D\) is a finite union, this becomes the active-branch system
\[T_X(\bar x)=\bigcup_{i\in I(z)}\{u:\nabla F(\bar x)u\in T_{D_i}(z)\}.\]
Thus a feasible tangent direction must satisfy the linearized constraint for at least one branch active at \(z\), and no inactive branch enters the system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under metric subregularity, feasible tangents are exactly the directions satisfying the linearized tangent condition for at least one active branch.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Branch Tangent Systems

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4 Sensitivity Analysis for Variational Systems p. 421

children.title: Normal-System Selection
children.top_down_role: Dependence of local normal information on active disjunctive branches.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-System Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limiting-normal selection for finite unions of closed branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the finite union \(C=\bigcup_{i=1}^m C_i\), every limiting normal to \(C\) at \(x\) belongs to the limiting normal cone of at least one active branch:
\[N_C(x)\subseteq\bigcup_{i\in I(x)}N_{C_i}(x).\]
Equality is not asserted: a normal to an individual active branch need not remain a normal after the other branches are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every limiting normal to a finite union can be assigned to an active branch, but not every active-branch normal must survive in the union.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_C(x)\subseteq\bigcup_{i\in I(x)}N_{C_i}(x)\).

children.title: Branch-Switching Singularity Family
children.top_down_role: Irregular local geometry where multiple active branches meet.

children.title: Branch-Collision Geometry
children.top_down_role: Local geometry at points shared by multiple active branches.

assumptions_latex: \(C=\bigcup_{i=1}^mC_i\) locally near \(x\), where each \(C_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is locally closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is a branch-collision point when \(T_{C_i}(x)\ne T_{C_j}(x)\) for some active \(i\ne j\).

notation.meaning: Branches active at the collision point.
Bouligand tangent cone of branch i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local definition based on collision of distinct active tangent branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The point \(x\in C\) is a branch-collision point if \(|I(x)|\ge2\) and there exist \(i,j\in I(x)\) with \(i\ne j\) and \(T_{C_i}(x)\ne T_{C_j}(x)\). Its first-order geometry is
\[T_C(x)=\bigcup_{i\in I(x)}T_{C_i}(x).\]
The collision is tangent-distinct when this union contains at least two unequal branch cones. This definition is representation-dependent unless the chosen branches are specified as part of the local set model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branch collision occurs where multiple modeled branches meet and at least two active branches have different tangent cones.
knowledge_statements.title: Branch-Collision Geometry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed definition is internally coherent but representation-dependent, and the generic variational-geometry citation does not establish that “branch-collision point” has this exact accepted meaning. A source explicitly defining the term or a documented local modeling convention is required.

children.title: Switching Geometry
children.top_down_role: Geometric changes caused by transitions between active branches.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_S(0,0)=S\), while away from the origin the tangent is the corresponding coordinate axis.

notation.meaning: Canonical switching set, the union of the two coordinate axes.
Bouligand tangent cone to the switching set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical scalar switching set without sign restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The switching set decomposes as \(S=(\mathbb{R}\times\{0\})\cup(\{0\}\times\mathbb{R})\). Its tangent cone is
\[T_S(a,b)=\begin{cases}\mathbb{R}\times\{0\},&a\ne0,\ b=0,\\ \{0\}\times\mathbb{R},&a=0,\ b\ne0,\\ S,&a=b=0.\end{cases}\]
Thus the origin is the switching singularity: both branches are active there, and the tangent cone is the nonconvex union of their tangent spaces. At every nonzero point only one branch remains locally active.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The canonical switching set is the union of two axes; its tangent is one axis off the origin and both axes at the switch.
knowledge_statements.title: Switching Geometry

children.title: Multi-Branch Tangent Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Competing tangent descriptions generated by simultaneous branch activity.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_C(x)=C\) is nonconvex, so no single active tangent space represents all feasible first-order directions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-axis counterexample exhibiting incompatible active tangent branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At \(x=(0,0)\), both branches are active and
\[T_{C_1}(x)=\mathbb{R}\times\{0\},\qquad T_{C_2}(x)=\{0\}\times\mathbb{R},\qquad T_C(x)=T_{C_1}(x)\cup T_{C_2}(x).\]
The directions \((1,0)\) and \((0,1)\) belong to \(T_C(x)\), but their midpoint \((1/2,1/2)\) does not. Hence the tangent cone is nonconvex, and selecting only one active branch omits valid tangent directions from the other branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two coordinate axes meeting at the origin yield a nonconvex tangent union, so any single-branch tangent description loses feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Branch Tangent Ambiguity

children.title: Normal Discontinuities at Switches
children.top_down_role: Abrupt changes in normal information near switching loci.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_C(0)=C\), whereas \(N_C(a,0)=\{0\}\times\mathbb R\) for \(a\ne0\) and \(N_C(0,b)=\mathbb R\times\{0\}\) for \(b\ne0\).

notation.meaning: Mordukhovich limiting normal cone to the set at the indicated point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A coordinate-cross model of the normal-cone jump at a branch switch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the closed union \(C=(\mathbb R\times\{0\})\cup(\{0\}\times\mathbb R)\), the limiting normal cone satisfies \(N_C(0)=C\). At every nonzero point of the horizontal branch, \(N_C(a,0)=\{0\}\times\mathbb R\), while at every nonzero point of the vertical branch, \(N_C(0,b)=\mathbb R\times\{0\}\). Thus approaching the switch along different branches yields different normal-cone limits, and the cone at the switch contains both branchwise families.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a coordinate cross, normals along either branch approach different axes, while the limiting normal cone at the switching point contains both axes.
knowledge_statements.title: Normal Discontinuities at Switches

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite Cartesian product of closed sets, tangent, regular-normal, and limiting-normal cones are the corresponding products of the factor cones.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\cap_iC_i}(x)=\cap_iT_{C_i}(x)\) and \(N_{\cap_iC_i}(x)=\sum_iN_{C_i}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex intersection rule under relative-interior qualification.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex sets with intersecting relative interiors admit exact tangent-intersection and normal-sum formulas at every feasible point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangential contact showing strict failure of the unqualified normal-sum rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sets satisfy \(C_1\cap C_2=\{(0,0)\}\). children.title: Mapping-Transport Geometry Calculus
children.top_down_role: Transport of tangent and normal systems through mappings.

children.title: Smooth Preimage Geometry
children.top_down_role: Local geometry inherited through smooth constraint mappings.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\), with \(\bar y=F(\bar x)\in D\).
\(D\subset\mathbb R^m\) is locally closed and normally regular at \(\bar y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{F^{-1}(D)}(\bar x)=\{h:\nabla F(\bar x)h\in T_D(\bar y)\}\) and \(N_{F^{-1}(D)}(\bar x)=\nabla F(\bar x)^TN_D(\bar y)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth inverse-image rule under normal regularity and transversality.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=F^{-1}(D)\). Under normal regularity and the stated transversality condition, \(C\) is normally regular at \(\bar x\), and its first-order geometry is the pullback of that of \(D\): \[T_C(\bar x)=\{h\in\mathbb R^n:\nabla F(\bar x)h\in T_D(\bar y)\},\qquad N_C(\bar x)=\nabla F(\bar x)^TN_D(\bar y).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under transversality and target-set regularity, a smooth preimage has the linearized tangent preimage and the adjoint pullback of target normals.

children.title: Linear Mapping Geometry Pair
children.top_down_role: Geometry transported through linear maps, kernels, and quotient representations.

children.title: Linear Image Geometry
children.top_down_role: Local geometry transported forward through a linear mapping.

assumptions_latex: \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty closed convex, and \(A(C)\) is closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{A(C)}(y)=\{v\in\mathbb R^m:A^Tv\in N_C(x)\}\).

notation.meaning: adjoint matrix of the linear mapping

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex normal representation for a closed linear image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(v\in\mathbb R^m\), the convex normal inequality on the image gives the equivalence \[v\in N_{A(C)}(y)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A^Tv\in N_C(x).\] Hence \(N_{A(C)}(y)=\{v\in\mathbb R^m:A^Tv\in N_C(x)\}\). The formula is independent of the chosen \(x\in C\cap A^{-1}(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector is normal to a closed convex linear image exactly when its adjoint pullback is normal to the original set at any preimage point.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Image Geometry

children.title: Linear Preimage Geometry
children.top_down_role: Local geometry pulled back through a linear mapping.

assumptions_latex: \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear and \(D\subset\mathbb R^m\) is nonempty closed convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex linear inverse-image calculus under range-relative-interior qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=A^{-1}(D)\). The range-relative-interior qualification yields the exact formulas \[T_C(x)=\{h\in\mathbb R^n:Ah\in T_D(Ax)\},\qquad N_C(x)=A^TN_D(Ax).\] Thus feasible first-order directions are precisely the linear preimages of target tangent directions, while every normal is an adjoint pullback of a target normal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a relative-interior qualification, a linear preimage has the tangent preimage and adjoint-pulled normal cone of the target set.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Preimage Geometry

children.title: Kernel-Induced Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Loss of directional information caused by nontrivial mapping kernels.

assumptions_latex: \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear with \(\ker A\ne\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every set \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) and every nonempty set \(K\subset\ker A\), one has \(A(C)=A(C+K)\); moreover, \(A^Tv\in(\ker A)^\perp\) for every \(v\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The kernel identifies the directions and normal components lost under imaging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any set \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) and any nonempty set \(K\subset\ker A\), one has \(A(C)=A(C+K)\). Hence geometry differing only along kernel fibers cannot be recovered from the image. Moreover, \(\operatorname{range}A^T=(\ker A)^\perp\), so every normal transported back from the image lies in \((\ker A)^\perp\) and contains no component parallel to \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nontrivial kernel erases all distinctions along its fibers, and image normals pull back only into the kernel's orthogonal complement.
knowledge_statements.title: Kernel-Induced Degeneracy

children.title: Quotient Representation Geometry
children.top_down_role: Geometric organization of linear images through quotient spaces.

assumptions_latex: \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear, \(K=\ker A\), and \(q:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n/K\) is the quotient map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=\widetilde A\circ q\), where \(\widetilde A:\mathbb R^n/K\to\operatorname{range}A\) is a linear isomorphism.

notation.meaning: induced linear isomorphism onto the range

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Factorization of linear geometry through the quotient by invisible directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\widetilde A(q(x))=Ax\). This is well defined and is a linear isomorphism from \(\mathbb R^n/K\) onto \(\operatorname{range}A\), with \[A=\widetilde A\circ q.\] If \(C=C+K\), then \(C=q^{-1}(q(C))\) and \(A(C)=\widetilde A(q(C))\). Thus the image geometry of a kernel-saturated set is exactly its quotient geometry transported by \(\widetilde A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every linear map factors through the quotient by its kernel; for kernel-saturated sets, image geometry is precisely transported quotient geometry.
knowledge_statements.title: Quotient Representation Geometry

children.title: Set-Valued Preimage Geometry
children.top_down_role: Constraint geometry represented through multifunctions and graphs.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\) has a locally closed graph near \((\bar x,0)\), and \(0\in F(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{F^{-1}(0)}(\bar x)=\bigcup_{v\in\mathbb R^m}D^*F(\bar x,0)(v)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=F^{-1}(0)=\{x:(x,0)\in\operatorname{gph}F\}\). Under the stated graph regularity and transversality, \[N_S(\bar x)=\{u:\text{there exists }v\in\mathbb R^m\text{ with }(u,-v)\in N_{\operatorname{gph}F}(\bar x,0)\}=\bigcup_{v\in\mathbb R^m}D^*F(\bar x,0)(v).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under graph regularity and transversality, normals to a generalized-equation solution set are exactly coderivative values over all multipliers.

children.title: Singular Mapping Geometry
children.top_down_role: Loss of geometric information under nonregular mappings.

assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is given by \(F(x)=x^2\), and \(D=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A zero derivative destroys the unqualified smooth normal pullback formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Here \(F^{-1}(D)=\{0\}\), and therefore \(N_{F^{-1}(D)}(0)=\mathbb R\). However, \(F'(0)=0\) and \(N_D(0)=\mathbb R\), giving \[F'(0)^TN_D(0)=\{0\}\ne\mathbb R=N_{F^{-1}(D)}(0).\] The transversality condition fails because \(N_D(0)\cap\ker F'(0)^T=\mathbb R\), so first-order pullback data misses every nonzero preimage normal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the squaring map over a singleton target, the derivative vanishes and predicts no nonzero normals, although the singleton preimage has every normal.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular Mapping Geometry

children.title: Smooth Image Geometry
children.top_down_role: Transport of local set geometry through smooth image mappings.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) is locally closed at \(\bar x\).
\(F:U\to V\) is a \(C^1\)-diffeomorphism between neighborhoods of \(\bar x\) and \(\bar y=F(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{F(C)}(\bar y)=DF(\bar x)T_C(\bar x)\) and \(N_{F(C)}(\bar y)=DF(\bar x)^{-T}N_C(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local diffeomorphic transport of Bouligand tangents and limiting normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\) be locally closed at \(\bar x\), and let \(F:U\to V\) be a \(C^1\)-diffeomorphism between neighborhoods of \(\bar x\) and \(\bar y=F(\bar x)\). Then smooth coordinate transport preserves the local variational geometry:
\[
T_{F(C)}(\bar y)=DF(\bar x)T_C(\bar x),\qquad N_{F(C)}(\bar y)=DF(\bar x)^{-T}N_C(\bar x).
\]
The same normal transformation holds for the regular normal cone. All image and inverse-image operations here are restricted to the stated neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local smooth change of coordinates maps tangent directions by its Jacobian and limiting normals by the inverse-transposed Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Image Geometry

children.title: Set-Valued Image Geometry
children.top_down_role: Image geometry arising from multifunctions or parameterized set mappings.

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Valued Image Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided image calculus through the restricted graph; equality needs additional lifting hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\), let \(F:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\), and fix \(\bar y\in F(C)\). Define \(F_C\) by \(\operatorname{gph}F_C=\operatorname{gph}F\cap(C\times\mathbb R^m)\). Then
\[
\bigcup_{\bar x\in C\cap F^{-1}(\bar y)}DF_C(\bar x,\bar y)(\mathbb R^n)\subset T_{F(C)}(\bar y).
\]
The reverse inclusion requires an additional condition ensuring compatible, convergent, or uniformly controlled preimage lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every tangent direction obtained from a restricted graphical lift is tangent to the set-valued image; recovering every image tangent requires an additional lift-stability condition.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^n\), \(F:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\), and \(\bar y\in F(C)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \bigcup_{\bar x\in C\cap F^{-1}(\bar y)}DF_C(\bar x,\bar y)(\mathbb R^n)\subset T_{F(C)}(\bar y)\); the reverse inclusion is not asserted without a lift-stability condition.

children.title: Branchwise Set Calculus
children.top_down_role: Assembly rules for branchwise tangent and normal systems.

children.title: Finite-Union Tangent Calculus
children.top_down_role: Branchwise tangency for finite unions.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Union Tangent Calculus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Bouligand tangent rule for a finite union whose branches are locally closed relative to the reference neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=\bigcup_{i=1}^r C_i\subset\mathbb R^n\), where \(r<\infty\), and fix \(\bar x\in C\). Assume that there is a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) such that every \(C_i\cap U\) is closed in \(U\). With \(I(\bar x)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}:\bar x\in C_i\}\),
\[
T_C(\bar x)=\bigcup_{i\in I(\bar x)}T_{C_i}(\bar x).
\]
No convexification of the right-hand side is part of this formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite union of branches that are closed in a common neighborhood of the point, the Bouligand tangent is exactly the union of the active branch tangent cones.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\in C\), and every \(C_i\) is closed relative to some common neighborhood of \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_C(\bar x)=\displaystyle\bigcup_{i\in I(\bar x)}T_{C_i}(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: active branch indices at the reference point

children.title: Finite-Union Normal Calculus
children.top_down_role: Regular, limiting, and convexified normals for finite unions.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Union Normal Calculus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regular, limiting, and closed-convexified normal rules for a locally closed finite union.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=\bigcup_{i=1}^r C_i\subset\mathbb R^n\), where \(r<\infty\), and fix \(\bar x\in C\). Assume that there is a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) such that every \(C_i\cap U\) is closed in \(U\). For \(I(\bar x)=\{i:\bar x\in C_i\}\),
\[
\widehat N_C(\bar x)=\bigcap_{i\in I(\bar x)}\widehat N_{C_i}(\bar x),
\]
\[
N_C(\bar x)\subset\bigcup_{i\in I(\bar x)}N_{C_i}(\bar x),
\qquad
N_C^c(\bar x)\subset\operatorname{clco}\!\left(\bigcup_{i\in I(\bar x)}N_{C_i}(\bar x)\right).
\]
The latter inclusions can be strict at branch collisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a locally closed finite union, regular normals intersect across active branches, while limiting and closed-convexified normals satisfy branchwise upper bounds that can be strict.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\in C\), and every \(C_i\) is closed relative to some common neighborhood of \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat N_C(\bar x)=\bigcap_{i\in I(\bar x)}\widehat N_{C_i}(\bar x)\), \(N_C(\bar x)\subset\bigcup_{i\in I(\bar x)}N_{C_i}(\bar x)\), and \(N_C^c(\bar x)\subset\operatorname{clco}\!\left(\bigcup_{i\in I(\bar x)}N_{C_i}(\bar x)\right)\).

notation.meaning: closed convexification of the limiting normal cone

children.title: Disjunctive Calculus Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Failure of exact branchwise calculus at switching and collision points.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Calculus Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Collision example showing strictness of the branchwise limiting-normal bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In \(\mathbb R^2\), let \(C_1=\{(u,v):v\ge 0\}\), \(C_2=\{(u,v):v\le 0\}\), and \(C=C_1\cup C_2=\mathbb R^2\). At \(\bar x=(0,0)\),
\[
N_C(\bar x)=\{0\},
\]
whereas
\[
N_{C_1}(\bar x)=\{(0,\beta):\beta\le 0\},
\qquad
N_{C_2}(\bar x)=\{(0,\beta):\beta\ge 0\}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
N_C(\bar x)\subsetneq N_{C_1}(\bar x)\cup N_{C_2}(\bar x)=\{0\}\times\mathbb R.
\]
Thus the branchwise limiting-normal inclusion cannot generally be replaced by equality at a branch collision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two opposite half-planes unite to form the plane, whose normal is zero, although the union of the two branch normals is a full line.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_C(\bar x)=\{0\}\subsetneq N_{C_1}(\bar x)\cup N_{C_2}(\bar x)=\{0\}\times\mathbb R\).

children.title: Piecewise-Smooth Tangent Calculus
children.top_down_role: Branchwise organization of tangent geometry for piecewise-smooth sets.

assumptions_latex: \(C=\bigcup_{i=1}^r M_i\), where each active \(M_i\subset\mathbb R^n\) is locally \(\{x:h_i(x)=0\}\).
Each \(h_i\) is \(C^1\) and \(Dh_i(\bar x)\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_C(\bar x)=\bigcup_{i\in I(\bar x)}\ker Dh_i(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: local defining map for branch i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite unions of regularly defined smooth equality branches.

source_refs.source_title: Finite-Dimensional Variational Inequalities and Complementarity Problems, Vol. II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(C=\bigcup_{i=1}^r M_i\), and every branch active at \(\bar x\) has a local representation \(M_i=\{x:h_i(x)=0\}\), where \(h_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_i}\) is \(C^1\) and \(Dh_i(\bar x)\) has full row rank. Then
\[
T_{M_i}(\bar x)=\ker Dh_i(\bar x)
\]
and the finite-union rule yields
\[
T_C(\bar x)=\bigcup_{i\in I(\bar x)}\ker Dh_i(\bar x),
\qquad I(\bar x)=\{i:\bar x\in M_i\}.
\]
This tangent is generally nonconvex at a switching point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many regular smooth equality branches, the tangent is the union of the kernels of the active branch Jacobians.

children.title: Piecewise-Smooth Normal Calculus
children.top_down_role: Branchwise organization of normal geometry for piecewise-smooth sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Smooth Normal Calculus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal formulas for finite unions of regular smooth equality branches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=\bigcup_{i=1}^r M_i\), where every branch active at \(\bar x\) is locally represented by \(M_i=\{x:h_i(x)=0\}\). Assume that \(h_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_i}\) is \(C^1\) and \(Dh_i(\bar x)\) has full row rank. Then
\[
N_{M_i}(\bar x)=\widehat N_{M_i}(\bar x)=\operatorname{range}Dh_i(\bar x)^T,
\]
and, with \(I(\bar x)=\{i:\bar x\in M_i\}\),
\[
\widehat N_C(\bar x)=\bigcap_{i\in I(\bar x)}\operatorname{range}Dh_i(\bar x)^T,
\qquad
N_C(\bar x)\subset\bigcup_{i\in I(\bar x)}\operatorname{range}Dh_i(\bar x)^T.
\]
The limiting-normal inclusion can be strict at branch collisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regular normals intersect the active smooth branch normal spaces, while limiting normals lie in their union, possibly strictly.
assumptions_latex: \(C=\bigcup_{i=1}^r M_i\), with every branch active at \(\bar x\) locally given by \(M_i=\{x:h_i(x)=0\}\).
Each \(h_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_i}\) is \(C^1\), and \(Dh_i(\bar x)\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat N_C(\bar x)=\bigcap_{i\in I(\bar x)}\operatorname{range}Dh_i(\bar x)^T\) and \(N_C(\bar x)\subset\bigcup_{i\in I(\bar x)}\operatorname{range}Dh_i(\bar x)^T\).

children.title: Geometric Lift Representation Family
children.top_down_role: Equivalent lifted representations used to expose set geometry.

children.title: Graphical Lifts
children.top_down_role: Set geometry represented through graphs of mappings and relations.

knowledge_statements.title: Graphical Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representing a set-valued inverse image as a coordinate projection of a graph intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F:\mathbb R^n\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^m\) and \(D\subset\mathbb R^m\), define
\[
L=\operatorname{gph}F\cap(\mathbb R^n\times D).
\]
Then
\[
F^{-1}(D)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:F(x)\cap D\ne\varnothing\}=\pi_x(L).
\]
For every \((\bar x,\bar y)\in L\),
\[
\pi_x\bigl(T_L(\bar x,\bar y)\bigr)\subset T_{F^{-1}(D)}(\bar x).
\]
Equality requires an additional condition ensuring compatible lifts of projected tangent sequences near \(\bar y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set-valued inverse image is the projection of the mapping graph intersected with the target set, and every tangent at a specified lift projects to an inverse-image tangent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^{-1}(D)=\pi_x(L)\), and for every \((\bar x,\bar y)\in L\), \(\pi_x(T_L(\bar x,\bar y))\subset T_{F^{-1}(D)}(\bar x)\).

children.title: Auxiliary-Variable Lift Family
children.top_down_role: Geometric consequences of equivalent lifted constraint systems.

children.title: Slack-Variable Lifts
children.top_down_role: Lifted set representations built by exposing inequality slack.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=\pi_x\{(x,s):g(x)+s=0,\ s\in\mathbb R_+^m\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise inequality constraints represented by nonnegative slack variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and interpret \(g(x)\le0\) componentwise. The inequality set \(S=\{x:g(x)\le0\}\) is represented exactly by
\[
L=\{(x,s)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R_+^m:g(x)+s=0\},
\qquad S=\pi_x(L).
\]
For every \(x\in S\), the compatible slack is unique and equals \(s=-g(x)\). If \(g\) is \(C^1\), any tangent \((v,w)\in T_L(x,s)\) necessarily satisfies
\[
Dg(x)v+w=0,
\qquad w\in T_{\mathbb R_+^m}(s).
\]
Sufficiency of these linearized conditions requires an appropriate constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth inequality system is exactly the projection of an equality system with a unique nonnegative slack; lifted tangents satisfy its linearized equality.
knowledge_statements.title: Slack-Variable Lifts

children.title: General Auxiliary-Variable Lifts
children.top_down_role: Equivalent higher-dimensional representations using additional latent variables.

knowledge_statements.title: General Auxiliary-Variable Lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existential constraints represented as projections of higher-dimensional feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(\Phi:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R^q\) and \(K\subset\mathbb R^q\), define
\[
L=\{(x,z)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^p:\Phi(x,z)\in K\}
\]
and
\[
S=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\exists z\in\mathbb R^p\text{ such that }\Phi(x,z)\in K\}.
\]
Then \(S=\pi_x(L)\). For every \((\bar x,\bar z)\in L\),
\[
\pi_x\bigl(T_L(\bar x,\bar z)\bigr)\subset T_S(\bar x).
\]
The reverse inclusion requires an additional lift-stability condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An existential constraint is exactly the projection of its auxiliary-variable feasible set, and every tangent at a specified lift projects to an original-space tangent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S=\pi_x(L)\), and for every \((\bar x,\bar z)\in L\), \(\pi_x(T_L(\bar x,\bar z))\subset T_S(\bar x)\).

children.title: Lift Equivalence Geometry
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between original feasible geometry and its lifted representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Lift Equivalence Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent-normal equivalence under a locally unique smooth graph lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\subset\mathbb R^n\) be locally closed at \(\bar x\), and suppose that near \((\bar x,\bar z)\),
\[
L=\{(x,\psi(x)):x\in S\},
\qquad \bar z=\psi(\bar x),
\]
where \(\psi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) is \(C^1\). Then
\[
T_L(\bar x,\bar z)=\{(v,D\psi(\bar x)v):v\in T_S(\bar x)\},
\]
and
\[
N_L(\bar x,\bar z)=\{(u-D\psi(\bar x)^Tq,q):u\in N_S(\bar x),\ q\in\mathbb R^p\}.
\]
Thus a locally unique smooth graph lift preserves the original tangent geometry and transforms limiting normals by the graph Jacobian and free conormal coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally unique smooth graph lift preserves tangents exactly and transforms limiting normals by the graph Jacobian together with free conormal components.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subset\mathbb R^n\) is locally closed at \(\bar x\).
Locally, \(L=\{(x,\psi(x)):x\in S\}\), where \(\psi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) is \(C^1\), and \(\bar z=\psi(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_L(\bar x,\bar z)=\{(v,D\psi(\bar x)v):v\in T_S(\bar x)\}\) and \(N_L(\bar x,\bar z)=\{(u-D\psi(\bar x)^Tq,q):u\in N_S(\bar x),\ q\in\mathbb R^p\}\).

children.title: Projection-Induced Artifacts
children.top_down_role: Geometric features introduced or obscured when lifted sets are projected.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Induced Artifacts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fold projection creates projected tangents absent from the tangent projection at its unique reference lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
L=\{(x,z)\in\mathbb R^2:x=z^2\},
\qquad S=\pi_x(L)=[0,\infty).
\]
At the unique lift \((0,0)\) of \(0\),
\[
T_L(0,0)=\{(0,w):w\in\mathbb R\},
\qquad \pi_x(T_L(0,0))=\{0\},
\]
whereas
\[
T_S(0)=\mathbb R_+.
\]
Therefore
\[
\pi_x(T_L(0,0))\subsetneq T_S(0).
\]
This fold projection has nonzero projected-set tangent directions that are absent from the projection of the tangent cone at its unique reference lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the vertex of a lifted parabola, all lifted tangents are vertical, but the projected half-line has nonzero positive tangents.
assumptions_latex: The reference lift is \((\bar x,\bar z)=(0,0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_x(T_L(0,0))=\{0\}\subsetneq T_S(0)=\mathbb R_+\).
